summary: Static assessment of firestore.rules only: client writes are denied on every collection; private player state is unreadable to clients; public views require owner identity, server-maintained parent linkage or a trusted admin claim; membership and room-view reads require the corresponding identity or membership. This is not a production security certification: emulator and deployed-rule enforcement have not been verified, and callable authorization, guardian identity and abuse protections require separate work.
scope: The tracked firestore.rules source, not the complete application or deployed Firebase project.

verification.method: Static source review against firebase-security-rules-auditor checklist
verification.deployedRules: not verified; current owner CLI authorization returned HTTP 401
verification.updateBypass: No client create/update/delete permission is granted.
verification.authority: Admin claim is token-based; parent/member arrays are written only through the server.
verification.businessAccess: Expected owner, linked parent, admin and member read paths exist. Actual query behavior needs emulator tests.
verification.typeAndSizeLimits: Direct writes are denied, so client field/type/size mutation is denied by these rules. Admin SDK writes bypass rules and require server validation and bounded collection growth.
verification.ownership: Every client-readable path checks authenticated UID, trusted claim or server-maintained linkage. All other paths default to deny.
